content.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame announces 2026 inductees
content.text: CLEVELAND, Ohio - The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame announced its class of 2026 on “American Idol” on Monday night. Your 2026 Rock Hall Performer Inductees are: Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross and the Wu-Tang Clan.To be eligible for induction, an individual artist or band must have released its first commercial recording at least 25 years prior to the year of nomination. Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan are first-time nominees. Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Oasis, and Sade are all multiple nominees. Collins has been added to the ranks of artists inducted as solo acts and with a band. Ozzy Osbourne and guitarists Jeff Beck and Eric Clapton are among them. Now Collins, already in the Hallowed Hall of Rock as a member of Genesis, joins them.The Induction ceremony will once again take place at The Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles on Saturday, November 14. Interestingly, the Rock Hall and Disney folks are going “old-school” with the ceremony this year. For the first time in three years, the ceremony won’t be a live stream or simulcast. Rather, it will be taped, presumably edited and later aired on the usual Disney properties sometime in December.Invested fans may also have noticed that the previously stated location rotation, which had Cleveland alternate between Los Angeles and New York, has apparently been suspended. But, before area music fans start gathering their rock-stuffed pierogies and ground-pork-and-broken-glass kielbasa to hurl at any visiting Rock Hall Foundation officials, the official press release promises the ceremony will return to Cleveland in 2027.The other award categories are an interesting mix of influential musicians and important industry figures. Queen Latifah will be inducted into the Rock Hall this year as an early influence. Here Latifah arrives at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in Los Angeles. (Photo by Evan Agostini/Invision/AP)Evan Agostini/Invision/APThe Early Influence Award– for artists whose music and performance style have directly influenced, inspired, and evolved rock & roll and music impacting culture– will go to Cuban and Latin music icon, singer Celia Cruz, influential Nigerian Afrobeat progenitor Fela Kuti, country-rock innovator Gram Parsons and pioneering emcees Queen Latifah and MC Lyte. The Musical Excellence Award is given to “artists, musicians, songwriters and producers whose originality and influence have had a dramatic impact on music.” This year’s inductees are mostly a posthumous producer-heavy group who are well known to album-credit-reading nerds, led by songwriter-producer-background singer Linda Creed, who co-wrote indelible hits including “The Greatest Love of All” and “Betcha By Golly Wow,” and died in 1986. Music production legend Arif Mardin, who died in 2004, has an impressive array of credits that include beloved songs and albums by Chaka Khan, Aretha Franklin, David Bowie, Willie Nelson, and many more, and will also be feted. Also being inducted is the late Jimmy Miller, who produced several classic Rolling Stones albums, including “Let It Bleed,” and “Beggars Banquet,” as well as albums by Traffic, Blind Faith and Motorhead before his death in 1994. The only surviving producer on the list is Rick Rubin, known for his seminal work in hip hop with Run DMC, The Beastie Boys and LL Cool J, along with many rockers and legends, including Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slayer and Johnny Cash. Finally, the 2026 Ahmet Ertegun Award will go to legendary television variety show host Ed Sullivan, whose variety show aired for 23 years and where much of the United States first saw bands such as The Beatles, The Rolling Stones and The Doors. ● Phil Collins - The first ballot songwriting-singing drummer or, if you ask him, a drummer who sings and writes songs, is, of course, already in as part of 70s art-rockers turned 80s pop-rockers, Genesis. His 80s solo albums (several of which were released while doing double duty in Genesis) were multi-hit and multi-platinum collections, particularly the 12 million domestic selling third album, “No Jacket, Required,” earning him a gaggle of industry awards, including eight Grammys, an Oscar, a couple of Golden Globes and is a member of the Songwriters Hall of Fame. Collins’ health has been in decline for several years and he can no longer play drums. So, good on the Rock Hall for not waiting until after he died to honor him. It should be a fun, cheeky speech if he can make it to the ceremony. Must Hear Music: “Face Value” (album, 1981), “I Don’t Care Anymore” (1982), “No Jacket Required” (album, 1985)● Billy Idol (Billy Idol, Steve Stevens) - The snarly-lipped ex-punk rocker hit it big in the 80s with guitarist and songwriting partner Stevens by writing and recording catchy anthemic rock and pop radio ready tunes and looking like he was born to be on MTV. Must Hear Music: “White Wedding,” “Dancing With Myself (1982) “Rebel Yell,” (album, 1983), “Cradle of Love” (1990)● Iron Maiden (Clive Burr, Paul Di’Anno, Bruce Dickinson, Janick Gers, Steve Harris, Nicko McBrain, Dave Murray, Adrian Smith, Dennis Stratton, Blaze Bayley - At last the Rock Hall voters throw up the two-pronged horn salute for one of the most influential bands in hard rock and heavy metal history. Their first four albums resonated with headbangers on all continents and the band is still going on stages and in the studio. Also, I’d wager, it was at the behest of bassist/songwriter/leader Harris to add singer Blaze Bayley, whose tenure with the band was relatively short and not terribly popular with many fans to the inductee list. Good job, Steve.Must Hear Music: “Iron Maiden” (1980), “Killers (1981), “The Number of The Beast (1982), “The Trooper” (1983), “Two Minutes to Midnight (1984) ● Joy Division/New Order (Ian Curtis, Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook, Stephen Morris, Gillian Gilbert - The third time has proven to be the charm for this seminal post-punk and dark wave band that morphed into a seminal UK post-punk and proto-EDM dance band. New Order had more commercial hits than its predecessor, but the dark DNA of Joy Division can be heard in New Order’s danceable grooves. It’ll be interesting to see who shows up to play as the surviving Joy Division/New Order principles. Sumner, Hook and Morris, haven’t always gotten along in the press or the courts. Sumner, Morris and Gilbert have been recording and touring as New Order since reforming in 2011 after settling a royalty dispute with Hook, so perhaps they can all play nice for a night. Must Hear Music: “She’s Lost Control” (1979), “Love Will Tear Us Apart” (1980), “Substance (album, 1988), “Blue Monday” (1983), “Bizarre Love Triangle” (1986), “Regret” (1993)Billy Idol coming to Blossom in September Rock Hall Nominations 2026: Why The Wu-Tang Clan mattersRock Hall Nominations 2026: Why New Edition mattersRock Hall Nominations 2026: Why INXS matters● Oasis (Gem Archer, Paul Arthurs, Andy Bell, Liam Gallagher, Noel Gallagher, Tony McCarroll) - The unfailingly confident, Mancunian Gallagher brothers and their bandmates are likely to deliver the most cheeky speeches of the evening as, not giving a flip about things such as halls of fame with singer Liam Gallagher having previously said the Rock Hall was “full of BUMBACLARTS” and was “for Wankers” on social media. Though when asked what they’d do if inducted, he answered, “Obv go and say it’s the best thing EVER.” The band grew from up-and-coming alt-rock stars to crossover, brit-pop rock gods and were massive and influential in their homeland and bona fide rock stars on this side of the pond too as their first two albums, “Definitely Maybe” and “What’s The Story Morning Glory,” both sold more than 12 million copies with the latter reaching 18 million worldwide. Their 2025 reunion tour was wildly successful, whetting fans’ appetite for more from the formerly famously battling brothers.Must Hear Music: “Cigarettes and Alcohol” (1994), “Rock N’ Roll Star,” “What’s The Story Morning Glory” (album, 1996), “D’You Know What I Mean?” (1997) “All Around The World” (1997)● Sade (Sade Adu, Paul Denman, Andrew Hale, Stuart Matthewman) - The beloved, sultry, smoky-voiced singer-songwriter and her eponymously titled band’s catalog of six studio albums is relatively small considering their debut, “Diamond Life” was released in 1984. But across the ensuing decades, those least platinum-selling albums with singles including “Sweetest Taboo,” “Paradise,” and “No Ordinary Love,” has made Sade one of those artists with fiercely loyal fans who are willing to wait for any melodic utterance from the reticent, and seldom publicly seen star. Sade fans would obviously be ecstatic if she were to perform, but they should probably just hope she bothers to show up at all. Either way, expect some veteran heavy hitters to induct and perform her songs. Sade delighted her fans by releasing, the quiet, meditative “Young Lion,” an ode to her trans son and her first new song in eight years.Must Hear Music: “Smooth Operator” (1984), “The Sweetest Taboo (1985), “Stronger Than Pride” (album, 1988), “No Ordinary Love” (1992), “Cherish The Day” (1993)● Luther Vandross - A worthy first timer and frankly, for me at least, a pleasant surprise. Vandross is an icon of black pop music as a singer-songwriter and producer and though he seemingly never quite received the crossover success he wanted, he is beloved and venerated by a couple of generations of R&B and soul, and soulful pop fans and singer-songwriters. “Lutha” will also likely have some big-name singers inducting and performing on his behalf. Must Hear Music: “Never Too Much” (1981), “So Amazing” (1983), “Give Me The Reason” (1986), “Here and Now (1989), “Dance With My Father (2003) ● Wu-Tang Clan (RZA, GZA, Ol’ Dirty Bastard, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, Inspectah Deck, U-God, Masta Killa, Cappadonna) - Surprisingly not the largest number of group members to be inducted (Parliament-Funkadelic still leads with 16 signatures on their official Rock Hall plaque), but definitely one of the more unique. The combination of emcees and personalities that producer-mastermind RZA managed to coalesce into a group is impressive on its own. But the group’s uncompromising, gritty New York sound jumped across all sorts of pop music and pop culture barriers to make them one of the most influential hip hop acts ever. Must Hear Music: “Enter The Wu-Tang” (album 1993), “Triumph” (1997), “Gravel Pit, (2000)
